title: Frontend TLS: Strong Cipher Suites Only, TLS 1.2+ with Post-Quantum Key Exchange (Grade A)
description: nmap ssl-enum-ciphers confirms frontend supports only TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3 with Grade A cipher suites. TLS 1.0 and 1.1 are disabled. TLS 1.3 uses post-quantum X25519MLKEM768 key exchange. No weak ciphers detected.
evidence_safe: nmap ssl-enum-ciphers on port 443: TLS 1.2 (4 ECDHE/DHE-only A-grade ciphers), TLS 1.3 (X25519MLKEM768 post-quantum). Overall least strength: A.

title: Backend TLS: TLS 1.2+ Only, Valid Microsoft Azure Certificate, Expires Aug 25 2026
description: Backend enforces TLS 1.2+ (protocol_version alert on TLS 1.0/1.1). TLS 1.3 negotiates TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384 over x25519. Certificate issued by Microsoft Azure RSA TLS Issuing CA 04, valid until Aug 25 2026 (~117 days). No weak ciphers or legacy protocol support detected.
evidence_safe: openssl s_client TLS 1.3 OK: TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384/x25519. Cert: CN=livelystone-c1480484.westus2.azurecontainerapps.io, notAfter=Aug 25 23:59:59 2026 GMT. TLS 1.0/1.1 rejected with alert 70.

title: Backend Missing HSTS Header (Strict-Transport-Security not observed in unauthenticated response)
description: HTTP response to unauthenticated request returned HTTP 401 without a Strict-Transport-Security header. HSTS may be present on authenticated responses, but its absence on 401 means browsers may not cache the HSTS policy for first-time visitors who receive an error.
evidence_safe: curl -v https://revops-dev.livelystone-c1480484.westus2.azurecontainerapps.io returned HTTP/2 401 with no Strict-Transport-Security header in response.
